newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila to import at least 500,000T sugar in 97/98.
newsitem.headline: Manila to import at least 500,000T sugar in 97/98.

text.p: The Philippines is expected to import at least 500,000 tonnes of sugar for crop year 1997/1998 (September 1 to August 31 next year) to meet a projected local shortfall, Sugar Regulatory Administration chief Wilson Gamboa said on Wednesday.
"I expect the imports to come from Australia, Thailand and Brazil," Gamboa told Reuters in a phone interview.
Gamboa said he expected the current sugar glut in the domestic market due to over importation of cheaper sugar from other countries in the past several months to "evaporate" in August this year.
Domestic raw sugar output is expected to drop to 1.7 million tonnes in crop year 1997/1998 from the revised forecast of 1.8 million tonnes in the current crop year, he said.
On Tuesday, Gamboa said Philippine raw sugar prices have firmed up to an average 605 pesos per 50-kilo bag at the farm level compared with 530 pesos per bag three weeks ago.
Gamboa pegged local production cost of a 50-kilo bag of sugar at 488 to 500 pesos as against earlier estimates by sugar farmers of 627 pesos.
"Local sugar climate is improving after traders saw that the government was bent to arrest further decline of the prices because of the influx of imported sugar bought at dump prices," Gamboa said.
Gamboa has been severely criticised by farmers in the past few days for the steep drop in prices. The government had failed to avert a sugar glut that led to a steep drop in prices, they said.

Among the measures being worked out by the government to prevent a drop in sugar prices are plans to increase tariffs on importation of the commodity and intervention by the state-agency National Food Authority.
